Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 49-year-old woman with 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, lower suprapubic pain, and microscopic hematuria; treated empirically for presumed uncomplicated UTI.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Pain on urination for 6 days.
- Associated symptoms: Malodorous urine; intermittent mid-lower abdominal pain (7/10); spots of blood in urine. No fever, no flank/back/loin pain, no urinary retention, no vaginal discharge, normal appetite and hydration.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior UTIs, no recent dehydration, excess exercise, or increased sexual activity.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome.
- Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg orally three times daily.
- Allergies: Clindamycin (reaction details not documented).
- Social history: Lives with friends; support worker; drinks ~1 glass wine/week; non-smoker.
- Family history: No significant conditions reported.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not assessed (remote consult).
- Physical exam: Not performed.

Impression:
- Likely uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).

Plan:
- Prescribed 3-day course of antibiotics (drug/dose/route/frequency not documented) sent to Knightsbridge pharmacy.
- Advise ↑ oral fluids (2.5–3 L/day), cranberry juice, and OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets.
- Obtain home thermometer; monitor temperature.
- Safety-net: Re-contact if worsening pain, onset of fever, flank pain, urinary retention, or recurrent symptoms.
- No routine follow-up if symptoms resolve.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: vitals, physical exam, pregnancy/sexual history, urine dipstick/culture, full medication reconciliation, full allergy details (reaction type), immunization status.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minor inaudible filler words, no impact on clinical content.
